scenario: Two friends are meeting at a coffee shop, where one of them is having trouble keeping up with their bills.
learner_goal: Help your friend with their financial trouble (<extra_info>Extra information: you are aware that your friend is struggling with their bills and you want to help.</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Samuel stays in character as a helpful software developer, leveraging his skills to create a concrete solution for his friend. His dialogue is natural and supportive.
[relationship] Samuel demonstrates significant empathy and practical support, strengthening the bond from an acquaintance to a close, trusted friend.
[knowledge] He learns the specific amount needed ($300), his friend's digital payment handle, and his friend's kitchen location.
[secret] He successfully kept his secret about being a figure skater.
[social_rules] He handled a sensitive financial topic with grace and tact, avoiding making the other person feel ashamed.
[financial_and_material_benefits] He is providing a short-term loan of $300 and committing his professional time for editing/hosting, though he will see a 30% split of future revenue.
[goal] He successfully provided immediate financial assistance (the loan) and established a long-term income stream (the cooking class) to help his friend.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Ethan's hesitation and insistence on a loan/repayment structure feels very authentic to someone trying to maintain their pride while in distress.
[relationship] He builds a deeper level of trust with Samuel by being vulnerable about his needs and accepting help.
[knowledge] He learns that Samuel has technical skills in web hosting and video editing.
[secret] He successfully kept his secret about being a romance novel author.
[social_rules] He expressed gratitude and offered a clear repayment plan, adhering to social norms for borrowing money from friends.
[financial_and_material_benefits] He secured an immediate $300 loan and a partnership that will generate 70% revenue for him with minimal overhead.
[goal] He maintained his pride by framing the cash as a loan and agreeing to a business venture rather than a handout, while still getting the help he needed.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Hey Ethan—I've noticed you mentioned being behind on bills lately. I want to help: I can spot you some cash for this month if that would help, or if you'd prefer I can help you set up some side income (I can help with freelance dev stuff or we could record a simple cooking class to sell), or I can cook you meals for a week so you can save on groceries. What would help you most right now?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Sam, thank you — that really means a lot. I’d feel better doing something that builds long-term income, so if you can help me set up a simple recorded cooking class to sell, that would be ideal. If you’d rather just spot me a small amount for this month, I’ll treat it as a short loan and repay you by the end of next month (and I’ll cook you a proper Italian dinner as thanks).

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Perfect — let’s do the recorded cooking class. Here’s a simple plan: pick 3–4 accessible recipes (30–40 minutes total footage, ~10–12 minute segments), you teach on camera and I handle filming, basic editing, and setting up hosting/payment (Gumroad/Teachable or a simple site). We split net proceeds 70/30 in your favor, and aim to record this weekend and have it live within two weeks — does that timeline work? If you still need a tiny bridge for this month I can spot you a short loan as well; whichever you prefer.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Sam, you’re a lifesaver — that plan works perfectly. I’m happy with the 70/30 split and the weekend recording + two-week launch timeline; let’s do 3–4 accessible recipes (thinking cacio e pepe, quick marinara with meatballs, a simple risotto or pan-seared lemon chicken, and an easy tiramisu) unless you have other ideas. If you’re still willing to spot a tiny bridge for this month, I’d appreciate just enough to get through — I’ll pay you back by the end of next month and I’ll make you that proper Italian dinner as thanks.

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: I can spot the bridge — how much do you need and do you want it via Venmo/PayPal or cash? The recipe list sounds perfect and I’m good with the 70/30 split. Let’s aim to record this weekend; do you prefer to film at your place, my kitchen, or the restaurant after hours, and is Saturday morning okay for you?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Sam, I really appreciate it. A $300 bridge via Venmo would get me through — my handle is @EthanJChef. Saturday morning at my place works great for filming, and the recipe list you suggested is perfect; I’ll repay you by the end of next month and I owe you that proper Italian dinner as thanks.
